newsitem.title: ISRAEL: RESEARCH ALERT-Israel Chemicals a buy.
newsitem.headline: RESEARCH ALERT-Israel Chemicals a buy.

text.p: Ofek Securities and Investments, an Israeli brokerage, has rated Israel Chemicals a buy in a report released on Monday.

Analyst Ephraim Steinbruch estimated 1996 earnings would reach 0.21 shekel per share compared with a 0.07 shekel loss in 1995. He said in the report that this year's earnings were expected to reach 0.23 shekel per share.
The report, Ofeks' first ever on Israel Chemicals, said demand for the company's products was expected to grow mainly from India and China by four to eight percent annually in the coming years.
Israel Chemicals controls companies that manufacture fertilisers and chemicals in Israel's mineral-rich Dead Sea area.
"The group and its new owners have established trade relations in Far East markets. These ties will contribute to growth in the company's sales in these markets," the report said.

Industrialist Shoul Eisenberg acquired a controlling stake in Israel Chemicals through Israel Corp. from the Israeli government in 1995. Eisenberg has extensive business ties with the Far East, especially China.

Ofek said Israel Chemicals was seeking to cut manufacturing and operating costs. It also noted that since 90 percent of its earnings were in foreign currency, Israel Chemicals would benefit from the cointnued depreication of the Israeli shekel.
A government privatisation plan unveiled last month listed Israel Chemicals as one of one of the government-owned companies slated for sale this year.
